prose.hook: Lesotho sits entirely inside South Africa, a single enclave with no other neighbors and no coastline. More than 80% of the country lies above 1,800 meters, making it one of the most consistently high-altitude places on the continent.
prose.physicalGeography: The terrain is mostly highland, made up of plateaus, hills, and mountains, with over 80% of the country sitting above 1,800 meters. Being landlocked and entirely surrounded by South Africa, Lesotho's elevation defines nearly every aspect of its landscape.
prose.climate: The climate is temperate, with dry winters that run cool to cold and summers that are hot and wet. The country also experiences periodic droughts.
prose.economy: Lesotho is a lower middle-income economy fully surrounded by South Africa, a position that shapes its economic life. It faces dire poverty, an environmentally fragile setting, and lost urban jobs and income tied to COVID-19, alongside systemic corruption, even as it draws investment in key infrastructure and renewable energy. Its industries include food, beverages, textiles, apparel assembly, handicrafts, construction, and tourism, while exports feature diamonds, garments, wool, power equipment, and bedding.
prose.peopleAndCulture: Sesotho and English are both official languages, alongside Phuthi, Xhosa, and Zulu. The population is overwhelmingly Sotho, at 99.7%, with small other groups including Kwena, Nguni (Hlubi and Phuthi), and Zulu. Christianity dominates religious life, split between Protestant denominations (47.8%, including Pentecostal and Lesotho Evangelical) and Roman Catholics (39.3%), with smaller shares of other Christians, non-Christians, and those with no religion.
